1085:         z_est = np.log2(contingency.shape[1])
1086: 
1087:     score_under = 0.0
1088:     if z_ref > 0:
1089:         score_under = 1.0 - true_given_est / z_ref
1090: 
1091:     score_over = 0.0
1092:     if z_est > 0:
1093:         score_over = 1.0 - pred_given_ref / z_est
1094: 
1095:     f_measure = util.f_measure(score_over, score_under, beta=beta)
1096: 
1097:     return score_over, score_under, f_measure
1098: 
1099: 
1100: def vmeasure(
1101:     reference_intervals,
1102:     reference_labels,
1103:     estimated_intervals,
1104:     estimated_labels,
1105:     frame_size=0.1,
1106:     beta=1.0,
1107: ):
1108:     """Frame-clustering segmentation: v-measure
1109: 
1110:     Computes cross-entropy of cluster assignment, normalized by the
1111:     marginal-entropy.
1112: 
1113:     This is equivalent to `nce(..., marginal=True)`.
1114: 
1115:     Examples
1116:     --------
1117:     >>> (ref_intervals,
1118:     ...  ref_labels) = mir_eval.io.load_labeled_intervals('ref.lab')
1119:     >>> (est_intervals,
1120:     ...  est_labels) = mir_eval.io.load_labeled_intervals('est.lab')
1121:     >>> # Trim or pad the estimate to match reference timing
1122:     >>> (ref_intervals,
1123:     ...  ref_labels) = mir_eval.util.adjust_intervals(ref_intervals,
1124:     ...                                               ref_labels,
1125:     ...                                               t_min=0)
1126:     >>> (est_intervals,
1127:     ...  est_labels) = mir_eval.util.adjust_intervals(
1128:     ...     est_intervals, est_labels, t_min=0, t_max=ref_intervals.max())
1129:     >>> V_precision, V_recall, V_F = mir_eval.structure.vmeasure(ref_intervals,
1130:     ...                                                          ref_labels,
1131:     ...                                                          est_intervals,
1132:     ...                                                          est_labels)
1133: 
1134:     Parameters
1135:     ----------
1136:     reference_intervals : np.ndarray, shape=(n, 2)
1137:         reference segment intervals, in the format returned by
1138:         :func:`mir_eval.io.load_labeled_intervals`.
1139:     reference_labels : list, shape=(n,)
1140:         reference segment labels, in the format returned by
1141:         :func:`mir_eval.io.load_labeled_intervals`.
1142:     estimated_intervals : np.ndarray, shape=(m, 2)
1143:         estimated segment intervals, in the format returned by
1144:         :func:`mir_eval.io.load_labeled_intervals`.
1145:     estimated_labels : list, shape=(m,)
1146:         estimated segment labels, in the format returned by
1147:         :func:`mir_eval.io.load_labeled_intervals`.
1148:     frame_size : float > 0
1149:         length (in seconds) of frames for clustering
1150:         (Default value = 0.1)
1151:     beta : float > 0
1152:         beta for F-measure
1153:         (Default value = 1.0)
1154: 
1155:     Returns
1156:     -------
1157:     V_precision
1158:         Over-clustering score:
1159:         ``1 - H(y_est | y_ref) / H(y_est)``
1160: 
1161:         If `|y_est|==1`, then `V_precision` will be 0.
1162:     V_recall
1163:         Under-clustering score:
1164:         ``1 - H(y_ref | y_est) / H(y_ref)``
1165: 
1166:         If `|y_ref|==1`, then `V_recall` will be 0.
1167:     V_F
1168:         F-measure for (V_precision, V_recall)
1169:     """
1170:     return nce(
1171:         reference_intervals,
1172:         reference_labels,
1173:         estimated_intervals,
1174:         estimated_labels,
1175:         frame_size=frame_size,
1176:         beta=beta,
1177:         marginal=True,
1178:     )
1179: 
1180: 
1181: def evaluate(ref_intervals, ref_labels, est_intervals, est_labels, **kwargs):
1182:     """Compute all metrics for the given reference and estimated annotations.
1183: 
1184:     Examples
1185:     --------
1186:     >>> (ref_intervals,
1187:     ...  ref_labels) = mir_eval.io.load_labeled_intervals('ref.lab')
1188:     >>> (est_intervals,
1189:     ...  est_labels) = mir_eval.io.load_labeled_intervals('est.lab')
1190:     >>> scores = mir_eval.segment.evaluate(ref_intervals, ref_labels,
1191:     ...                                    est_intervals, est_labels)
1192: 
1193:     Parameters
1194:     ----------
1195:     ref_intervals : np.ndarray, shape=(n, 2)
1196:         reference segment intervals, in the format returned by
1197:         :func:`mir_eval.io.load_labeled_intervals`.
1198:     ref_labels : list, shape=(n,)
1199:         reference segment labels, in the format returned by
1200:         :func:`mir_eval.io.load_labeled_intervals`.
1201:     est_intervals : np.ndarray, shape=(m, 2)
1202:         estimated segment intervals, in the format returned by
1203:         :func:`mir_eval.io.load_labeled_intervals`.
1204:     est_labels : list, shape=(m,)
1205:         estimated segment labels, in the format returned by
1206:         :func:`mir_eval.io.load_labeled_intervals`.
1207:     **kwargs
1208:         Additional keyword arguments which will be passed to the
1209:         appropriate metric or preprocessing functions.
1210: 
1211:     Returns
1212:     -------
1213:     scores : dict
1214:         Dictionary of scores, where the key is the metric name (str) and
1215:         the value is the (float) score achieved.
1216:     """
1217:     # Adjust timespan of estimations relative to ground truth
1218:     ref_intervals, ref_labels = util.adjust_intervals(
1219:         ref_intervals, labels=ref_labels, t_min=0.0
1220:     )
1221: 
1222:     est_intervals, est_labels = util.adjust_intervals(
1223:         est_intervals, labels=est_labels, t_min=0.0, t_max=ref_intervals.max()
1224:     )
1225: 
1226:     # Now compute all the metrics
1227:     scores = collections.OrderedDict()
1228: 
1229:     # Boundary detection
1230:     # Force these values for window
1231:     kwargs["window"] = 0.5
1232:     (
1233:         scores["Precision@0.5"],
1234:         scores["Recall@0.5"],
1235:         scores["F-measure@0.5"],
1236:     ) = util.filter_kwargs(detection, ref_intervals, est_intervals, **kwargs)
1237: 
1238:     kwargs["window"] = 3.0
1239:     (
1240:         scores["Precision@3.0"],
